lens: Analog notebook warmth: paper textures, handwritten coach annotations on transcripts
name: Coach's Field Notebook
one_liner: A warm paper-and-ink training notebook: each call is an open spread with the coach writing in the margin, and every score is a ruled ledger line traceable to a transcript quote.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the analog lens for the live call, debrief, pre-call briefing and wizard intake: paper grain, ruled lines, a vermilion handwritten coach voice, stamped grades. Deviated in two places. The persona library and dashboards use a crisp grid, because Mobbin's library and dashboard references (Base44 templates, Klaviyo's goal-grouped library, Gumloop's score dashboard) scan faster without texture. Competitor positioning (Second Nature and Hyperbound, per their own and review blogs) centres on realistic practice and real-call scoring, so the notebook makes traceable, visible coaching the hero rather than decoration.

palette.use: Page background, with a faint SVG grain at 3-4% opacity on the page only
Primary text and the stamped primary button
Secondary text and caller (persona) lines in the transcript; 6.2:1 on paper
Ruled lines and hairline borders, decorative only
The rep's own lines and bubbles; 7.2:1 on paper
Coach margin notes and objection alerts; 4.7:1 on paper
Evidence highlighter behind quoted lines at 45% alpha; text stays ink
Criterion met and positive deltas; 5.0:1 on paper
Warnings, fallback-grader notice, weakest criterion; 5.1:1 on paper

design_language.typography: Fraunces (variable; optical size 72 for the landing headline, 24-36 for section titles and transcript headers). Instrument Sans 400/500/600 for UI and body, 16px minimum. Caveat 500 at 20-22px for coach margin notes only, never body copy. JetBrains Mono for timers, scores, weights and line numbers. Type scale 1.25.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Cards use a 6px radius and a 1px rule border with no drop shadow. Chips and toggles are pills. Index cards have a 2px radius and a faint ruled top line. Depth comes from a 1-2 degree tilt on sticky notes and grade stamps, plus ink-on-paper contrast, not elevation. Ruled-line backgrounds (28px rhythm) appear only on the transcript and talk-track pages.
design_language.motion: Coach notes write in with an ink-stroke reveal (about 600ms), one line at a time, without blocking the transcript. Rubric bars fill over 400ms with ease-out. The grade stamp lands with a short scale-and-settle (about 180ms). Checkboxes draw their tick with a stroke animation. Every motion has a static fallback under reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.5px stroke in ink or graphite. One hand-drawn accent (underline or circle) on headings and selected cards. No emoji in the UI.
design_language.theme_modes: Paper (light) is the default. Lamp-lit (dark): background #1A1814, sheet #23211B, text #EFE8D8, graphite #A39B89, rule #3A362D, rep-ink #8DB4E8, coach #F08A5D (7.2:1), highlight #E0B94A at 30%, sage #8CC596. Follows the system colour scheme with a manual toggle stored per viewer. Print renders the debrief as a clean white page with no grain or tilt.

navigation_and_ia: Top bar: small stamp wordmark, then Practice, Library, Progress and Team (Team shows only for org accounts), a Cmd+K palette and a New persona button. Routes: /library, /library/[slug], /new-persona, /call/[id]/briefing, /call/[id], /debrief/[id], /progress, /team. Library job families sit as paper index tabs across the top so a rep always sees which sales job they are in. Mobile: bottom tab bar (Practice, Library, Progress, More), hidden during a live call.

screens.layout: Split hero on paper. Left: Fraunces headline 'Rehearse the hard call on paper first', a two-line subhead, a stamped 'Start a practice call' button and an outline 'Browse 120 personas' button. Right: an open notebook spread, transcript left and coach margin right, with a Caveat note writing itself in. Below: three feature strips (live coaching, persona library, evidence-backed grades) and a model strip.
screens.key_components: Animated spread with a static PNG fallback for the README (light and dark). Badge row: MIT, Next.js 15, OpenAI Realtime, GPT-4.1 mini. 'Run it locally' card linking to setup. 'Good first issue' cards. Footer credit. The README mirrors the hero and adds an architecture diagram (voice, coach, grader) and a contributor table.
screens.change_vs_today: Replaces the blurry orb and four generic feature cards with a product-real spread that shows coaching and grading on the first screen. The README tells the same story, which is what fund reviewers read first.

screens.layout: Left rail (about 240px) with facets: sales job (15 families), industry, difficulty (1-3 dots), objection type and mode (voice or text). Main column: sticky header with search and result count ('132 personas'), job families as paper index tabs, then a grid of index cards: 3 across on desktop, 2 on tablet, 1 on phone.
screens.key_components: Index card: illustrated monogram avatar (no stock photos), persona name, role and company type, difficulty dots, top objection tag, length estimate, Practice and Duplicate actions. Active-filter chips with clear-all. Flip-to-see view shows talk track and rubric weights. Final tile: Build a new persona opens the wizard.
screens.change_vs_today: Today: a three-item select. Becomes a browsable catalogue of 120 seeded personas across 15 sales jobs. Facets follow the Base44 and Klaviyo library patterns, and the index card carries the notebook lens into the grid.

screens.layout: Six-step intake: a step rail on the left (Source, Persona, Scenario, Talk track, Rubric, Voice and test) and a live index card on the right that fills in as the model streams. Step 1 offers four source cards (job description, product URL, CRM notes or ICP, pasted call transcript) plus a file drop zone.
screens.key_components: Character counts and a 'what the model reads' disclosure per source. Typewriter streaming into the card. Inline pencil-edit on any field. Rubric weights auto-suggested from the source, adjusted with sliders that total 100. A 60-second test roleplay before save. Save to my library, or Open a pull request (writes the persona file into the repo's scenarios folder). Model badges: GPT-4.1 mini drafts, gpt-realtime voices.
screens.change_vs_today: Today there is no creation path beyond duplicating and editing a long form. This adds a guided intake modelled on PlayAI's stepper with live preview, ElevenLabs' short agent-creation form and HubSpot's source-picker step.

screens.layout: One spread. Left page: the briefing on ruled paper, with the persona index card, a 'You're talking to' line, the goal as a headline, and the talk track as a numbered checklist the rep can tick. Right page: setup card with a Voice and Text segmented control, coach mode (Silent, Whisper cues, Full coach), a mic check meter, and a large stamped Start call button.
screens.key_components: Difficulty and objection chips. 'What this persona will push on' list generated from the scenario. Rubric weights as a stacked bar labelled 'where points come from'. Last score for this persona in Caveat ('Last time 50. Pricing was thin.'). Keyboard hint: Space to start.
screens.change_vs_today: Today: a dropdown, a blurry orb and a collapsed talk track. The briefing says what will be scored and lets the rep choose how much coaching they get before the call starts.

screens.layout: Open spread at 1440px. Left page (about 60%): the transcript on ruled paper with line numbers in the margin; rep lines in rep-ink, caller lines in graphite. Right page: the coach margin (a stream of vermilion Caveat notes), a live rubric ledger with six criteria and pencil bars, and talk-track ticks. Footer: composer, mic toggle, next-question chips, and an ink 'End and grade'.
screens.key_components: Persona header with portrait, status ('Your turn' or 'Caller speaking') and a JetBrains Mono timer. Whisper pill in voice mode. Objection sticky note (tilted, highlight yellow) naming the objection and linking to the talk-track step. Ledger deltas (+4, -2) per turn, marked provisional. Footer shows 'Coach: gpt-4.1-mini, 0.8 s' so the model is visible.
screens.change_vs_today: Today: a chat app with a drawer and no feedback until the end. Becomes a coaching surface where each turn gets a margin note and a score delta, objections raise a sticky note, and the coach never speaks in the persona's voice.

screens.layout: Top: 'Call debrief' header with date and duration, a hand-stamped letter grade with the number in mono beneath, and a goal tick-list ('Goal: partly achieved'). Then two columns: 'What worked' with highlighted quotes, and 'Practise next' with one focus and a Caveat note. Below: the criterion ledger, then the transcript with coach notes in the margin beside each line that moved a score.
screens.key_components: Quote chips that jump to and flash the transcript line. Ledger rows with weight, score bar, rationale and quotes. 'Practise this persona again' stamped button. Print gives a clean paper page. Grader status shown as a notebook note: the current 'LLM grader failed, keyword heuristic used' case gets an explanation and a retry, not only a yellow bar.
screens.change_vs_today: Today: one long scroll with a score ring and bars. Becomes a review where every point traces to a quote and a transcript line, and the fallback state is explained rather than hidden.

screens.layout: Logbook. Top row: four stat tiles drawn with tally marks (sessions, average, best, minutes practised). Middle: a 12-week practice grid on ruled week lines. Bottom: score trend beside a mastery panel with six criterion sparklines and a 'practise next' callout naming the weakest criterion and the persona to run.
screens.key_components: Tally-mark streak counter. Milestone stamps (First objection handled, Five calls over 70, Pricing solved) with outlined locked states, modelled on Base44's levels checklist. 7d, 30d and all-time toggle. Export as PDF.
screens.change_vs_today: Today: four numbers and a plain list. Becomes a progress log that shows which criteria are improving and which persona to run next.

screens.layout: Coaching board. Top: team, job-family and date filters, a 'Needs review' queue and an 'Assign practice' action. Main: ledger table with one row per rep, six criterion cells banded sage, amber or vermilion, a six-week sparkline, last call and open notes count. Right drawer: the selected rep's latest debrief with supervisor notes in Caveat.
screens.key_components: Score cells show the number as well as the colour. Assign-persona flow with a due date. Supervisor note composer using the existing supervisor-notes data. CSV export. Org switcher in the top bar. A Plane-style widget row for team averages.
screens.change_vs_today: Today there is no manager surface, though the data model already has orgs and supervisor notes. Becomes a board that shows a team's weakest criterion and sends targeted practice, aimed at call centres and training firms.

screens.layout: 390px single column. Sticky top strip: persona name, status and timer. Under it, a one-line margin tape showing the latest coach note in Caveat; tap to open the full note sheet. Transcript fills the screen as one ruled column. A live score ring at top right opens the ledger as a bottom sheet. Bottom dock: push-to-talk stamp (voice) or composer (text), next-question chips, and a smaller ink 'End and grade'.
screens.key_components: Round in-call controls adapted from Telegram's call screen. 16px side gutters, no horizontal scroll. Header shows persona name only. 44px minimum touch targets and safe-area insets. The Next.js dev badge that now overlaps the timer is hidden in production builds. In text mode the keyboard sits above the dock.
screens.change_vs_today: Today the header truncates the title, End and grade crowds the bottom edge, and the coach has nowhere to speak. Becomes a single-column notebook with a margin tape and sheet-based scoring.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Three coach channels, one rule: the persona never sees coach output, so practice stays realistic. (1) Margin notes: text, always on, written beside the transcript line they refer to. (2) Whisper cue: a short pill in voice mode, visual only in v1 so the caller's speech cannot be confused with it. (3) Objection alert: a sticky note when the coach classifies price, timing, competitor, authority or trust objections, linked to the talk-track step. Rubric deltas refresh after each rep turn from a schema-validated coach call and stay marked provisional until the debrief re-grades. Target latency under 1.5s for text. As-is the app falls short here (no coaching, no live scoring). This design meets the standard only if the coach stream ships.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: 15 job families (SDR cold call, AE discovery, SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections), each with 8 or more seeded personas that carry an objection taxonomy, a rubric template and scripted replies. Facets: job, industry, difficulty, objection type, mode. Wizard: six steps from four source types to a schema-validated persona, then a test roleplay, then save or open a pull request. As-is there are 3 built-in scenarios and no wizard. This meets the standard only with roughly 120 quality personas and validated wizard output.
signature_moments: Coach notes write themselves in vermilion beside the transcript line they refer to.
The grade lands as an ink stamp, tilted a few degrees.
Index cards in the library: flip one to see its talk track and rubric.
The wizard's preview card fills in line by line as the model streams.
Every number in a debrief links to the exact transcript line it came from.
openai_fund_angle: Show OpenAI as the engine, not a logo. The live-call footer names each model and its latency (gpt-realtime for voice, gpt-4.1-mini for coach and grader). The landing page and README carry a How it uses OpenAI diagram. Settings lists the model for each role, with an override for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint so forks can swap models. Contributor invitations: Good first issue cards, persona pull requests from the wizard, a proposed AGENTS.md and Codex skill that drafts persona packs, and a CONTRIBUTING note on how maintainers use Codex for PR review. The persona gallery credits each contributor by GitHub handle.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (about 1 week): tokens, fonts and the Tailwind v4 move, with shadcn primitives copied in and a visual-regression baseline. Phase 1 (2 weeks): live call and debrief, the highest-value screens for the live coaching score, plus the coach stream backend. Phase 2 (2 weeks): library data model, facets and 40 seeded personas. Phase 3 (2 weeks): wizard, with the seed grown to 120. Phase 4 (2 weeks): pre-call briefing, progress dashboard, team view, mobile polish and print styles.

risks: Live scoring is only as good as the coach stream. Without a schema-validated, low-latency coach call, the live ledger will mislead; the current debrief already fell back to a keyword heuristic.
Paper texture and handwriting can read as retro or twee in an enterprise demo. Keep grain under 4% and use Caveat only for coach notes.
The 120-persona library is a content project, not a UI task. Seed quality drives the persona score.
Moving Tailwind v3 to v4 and copying components touches every screen; ship it as one branch with visual regression tests.
HeroUI is the alternative if faster defaults matter more than a custom paper look; choosing it gives up much of the notebook treatment.
The shadcn Base UI default claim and the competitor weaknesses come from vendor and third-party blogs; verify before using them in pitch copy.
